title: Obedience
definition: Obedience is the believer’s faithful response to God’s Word through trust, surrender, and Spirit-enabled action.
summary: Obedience is the believer’s faithful response to God’s Word through trust, surrender, and Spirit-enabled action.
christFocus: Jesus obeyed the Father perfectly and calls His disciples to follow Him in love, not to earn salvation but because they belong to Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Obedience is not the enemy of grace. Scripture teaches that believers are saved by grace and then called to walk in the good works God prepared for them.

Christian obedience flows from love for Christ and dependence on the Holy Spirit. It is not mere rule-keeping, image management, or fear of rejection; it is the fruit of a changed heart.

Jesus connects hearing with doing. Those who follow Him are called to put His words into practice in daily decisions, relationships, repentance, service, and worship.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people hear obedience and think of harsh religion or impossible pressure. Biblical obedience is different: Christ receives sinners by grace and then leads them into life-giving faithfulness.

This doctrine also challenges passive faith. The Word is meant to be lived, not merely admired.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask where Christ is calling you to obey today. Take one concrete step by the Spirit’s power, not to earn God’s love, but because you have already been loved and called by Jesus.
